import sys
from pathlib import Path

ROOT = Path(__file__).resolve().parent
CTX = "shared/references/tooling/context.md"

DESC = {
    "ranger/skills/audit": 'Use this, not a freehand code review, whenever code is hunted for bugs or vulnerabilities, a suspected bug needs proof, or a fix needs checking: "find bugs in this", "audit this for security issues", "is this really a bug", "did that fix resolve the finding". Rust, TypeScript, JavaScript, Python, Go. Refutes candidates, groups defect families, returns finding-report@2 and verdict@3.',
    "sentinel/skills/gate": 'Use this, not freehand checking, whenever an artifact must be verified before the next stage: "verify this", "is this done?", "check this spec/plan/requirement/PR", "does this meet the criteria?", "gate this", and before starting implementation, shipping or opening a PR. Not for Q&A, code explanation or exploration. Returns verdict@3: cleared, or blockers.',
    "muse/skills/component": 'Use this, not a freehand spec, whenever a UI component\'s behavior is specified, audited or checked for readiness: "spec this component", "write a spec for this design", "is this component spec ready?", "gate this component spec". Drafts, audits and gates a spec@1 covering props, variants, per-state behavior and accessibility.',
    "muse/skills/promote": 'Use when a chosen sketch option or a spike that worked should become real work: "promote this option", "let\'s build option B", "turn the chosen design into a requirement", "that spike worked, make it a feature". Turns an option-set@1 or spike-report@1 into a requirement@1 with the decision, render and what was not verified. The only route from exploration into the gated stages; it does not build, spec or plan.',
    "muse/skills/sketch": 'Use this, rather than describing options in prose, whenever the user wants to see options before deciding: "show me some options", "try a few directions", "sketch this", "what could this look like", "I want to see it before we spec it". Builds and renders three structurally different options as an option-set@1 with a decision log. Non-binding: no gate, spec or tests. Stops before implementing; use promote to build.',
    "scribe/skills/architect": 'Use when a finding-report@2, implementation-review@2 or implementation-result@1 identifies a structural defect class, or the same kind of defect keeps recurring: "make this class of bug impossible". Produces the smallest spec@1 that makes recurrence impossible or machine-detectable through a type, API, boundary, invariant, lint, test or CI rule.',
    "scribe/skills/audit-architecture": 'Use when a draft spec@1 should be checked against whole-system architecture before scribe/gate-spec: "check this spec against our architecture", "does this fit the system", "audit this against the arch model". Checks it against the persisted arch-model@2 (building or refreshing it if absent or stale) and returns specific rewritten fixes on fail.',
    "scribe/skills/audit-spec": 'Use this, not a freehand review, whenever a spec\'s quality is reviewed: "review this spec", "is this spec complete?", "audit this spec", "what is missing from this spec". Adversarially checks a spec@1 on its own terms for untestable criteria, ambiguity, missing error cases and scope overlap; returns issues with rewritten fixes.',
    "scribe/skills/correct-spec": 'Use, instead of editing the spec by hand, when implementation shows a spec criterion contradicts what the system does (a spec_contradiction from smith). Given spec_file_path, criterion_id and the contradiction report, returns a corrected spec@1 with revision_note set. For a spec that is wrong, not merely hard to satisfy.',
    "scribe/skills/draft-spec": 'Use this, not a freehand spec, whenever a spec is written or drafted: "spec this out", "draft a spec", "write a spec for this requirement", "write the acceptance criteria". Turns a requirement@1 and optional research-report@1 into a spec@1 with scope, non_goals, api_surface and testable criteria; error cases carry is_error_case: true. No TBDs.',
    "scribe/skills/gate-spec": 'Use this, not a freehand verdict, whenever a spec must be judged ready before planning: "gate this spec", "is this spec ready?", "check this spec before we plan it". Default disposition is fail. Checks the spec on its own terms and returns a verdict@3 with blockers specific enough for scribe/draft-spec to act on.',
    "scribe/skills/spec-drift": 'Use when asked whether implemented code still matches its spec, weeks or months later: "check spec drift", "does the code still match this spec?", "has this spec drifted?". Given spec_file_path and a workspace root, reports each criterion as covered, uncovered or drifted. On-demand diagnostic, not a gate.',
    "scribe/skills/verify-spec": 'Use when asked whether a spec matches its source: "is this grounded?", "does this spec match the requirement?", "check this spec against the requirement". Classifies each criterion of a draft spec@1 as supported, unsupported or overfitted against the requirement@1 and optional research-report@1. Evidence only, no verdict; run before implementation.',
}

CODEX_DESC = {
    "ranger/skills/audit": "Find evidence-backed reachable defects in Rust, TypeScript, JavaScript, Python, or Go. Use this, not a freehand code review, for bug hunts, security audits, suspected defects, or post-remediation verification; do not use for general code explanation.",
    "sentinel/skills/gate": "Independently verify an artifact against its criteria before it crosses a lifecycle boundary. Use this, not freehand checking, for “is this done?”, “verify this”, and readiness checks on requirements, specs, plans, implementations, and PRs.",
    "muse/skills/component": "Turn UI intent into an implementation-ready component specification. Use this, not a freehand spec, when the user asks to specify, audit, or gate a component design before planning or implementation.",
    "scribe/skills/draft-spec": "Draft a testable specification from a requirement and optional research evidence. Use this, not a freehand spec, for “draft a spec”, “spec this out”, or “write a spec for this requirement”.",
    "scribe/skills/audit-spec": "Adversarially review a spec for ambiguity, untestable criteria, missing error behavior, and scope defects. Use this, not a freehand review, for “audit this spec”, “is this spec complete?”, or before gate-spec.",
    "scribe/skills/gate-spec": "Issue the binding pass or fail decision for a specification before planning begins. Use this, not a freehand verdict, for “gate this spec”, “is this ready to plan?”, or “check this spec before implementation”.",
    "muse/skills/sketch": "Explore several structurally different options for a design or approach, rendered and shown before they are described, with a decision log. Use this, rather than describing options in prose, when the user wants to see options before deciding what to build. Non-binding: no gate, no spec, no tests.",
}

for key, text in DESC.items():
    p = ROOT / "plugins" / key / "SKILL.md"
    s = p.read_text()
    new, n = re.subn(
        r"(^description: >-\n)(.*?)(\nversion:)",
        lambda m: m.group(1) + "  " + text + m.group(3),
        s, count=1, flags=re.S | re.M,
    )
    assert n == 1, key
    p.write_text(new)

for key, text in CODEX_DESC.items():
    p = ROOT / "harnesses/codex/plugins" / key / "SKILL.md"
    s = p.read_text()
    new, n = re.subn(r"^description: .*$", lambda m: "description: " + text, s, count=1, flags=re.M)
    assert n == 1, key
    p.write_text(new)


def edit(rel, old, new):
    p = ROOT / rel
    s = p.read_text()
    assert s.count(old) == 1, (rel, old[:40])
    p.write_text(s.replace(old, new))


S = "Keep command output and scripts out of the thread as `shared/references/tooling/context.md` says."

# Claude skills
edit("plugins/ranger/skills/audit/SKILL.md",
     "Record unsupported or impractical checks as coverage gaps; do not imply coverage.",
     "Record unsupported or impractical checks as coverage gaps; do not imply coverage. " + S)
edit("plugins/sentinel/skills/gate/SKILL.md",
     "- [Verdict Schema](../../../../shared/schemas/verdict@3.json)",
     "- [Verdict Schema](../../../../shared/schemas/verdict@3.json)\n- [Context hygiene](../../../../shared/references/tooling/context.md) — keep command output and scripts out of the thread when running checks.")
edit("plugins/muse/skills/sketch/SKILL.md",
     "`shared/references/architecture/modes.md`, `shared/schemas/option-set@1.json`\n</references>",
     "`shared/references/architecture/modes.md`, `shared/schemas/option-set@1.json`\n\nWhen running render or build commands, " + S[0].lower() + S[1:] + " Look at one render at a time.\n</references>")
edit("plugins/scribe/skills/audit-architecture/SKILL.md",
     "`shared/schemas/spec@1.json`, `shared/schemas/arch-model@2.json`, `shared/schemas/arch-audit@1.json`\n</references>",
     "`shared/schemas/spec@1.json`, `shared/schemas/arch-model@2.json`, `shared/schemas/arch-audit@1.json`\n\n" + S + "\n</references>")
edit("plugins/scribe/skills/spec-drift/SKILL.md",
     "`shared/schemas/spec@1.json`\n</references>",
     "`shared/schemas/spec@1.json`\n\n" + S + "\n</references>")

# Codex skills
edit("harnesses/codex/plugins/ranger/skills/audit/SKILL.md",
     "Record uncovered risk as a coverage gap.", "Record uncovered risk as a coverage gap.\n- " + S)
edit("harnesses/codex/plugins/sentinel/skills/gate/SKILL.md",
     "- Treat a required check that has not finished as pending and fail the gate.",
     "- Treat a required check that has not finished as pending and fail the gate.\n- " + S)
edit("harnesses/codex/plugins/scribe/skills/spec-drift/SKILL.md",
     "- Do not modify implementation, tests, or the persisted spec during diagnosis.",
     "- Do not modify implementation, tests, or the persisted spec during diagnosis.\n- " + S)
edit("harnesses/codex/plugins/scribe/skills/audit-architecture/SKILL.md",
     "- Do not persist or overwrite the model without user authorization.",
     "- Do not persist or overwrite the model without user authorization.\n- " + S)
edit("harnesses/codex/plugins/muse/skills/sketch/SKILL.md",
     "never describe a render you did not see.",
     "never describe a render you did not see. " + S + " Look at one render at a time.")

# Agents
LF = "Load `" + CTX + "` before running commands or reading large inputs; keep output and scripts out of your result."
for rel in ["ranger/agents/scanner", "ranger/agents/boundary-tracer", "ranger/agents/adversary"]:
    p = ROOT / "plugins" / (rel + ".md")
    s = p.read_text()
    assert s.count("</load_first>") == 1, rel
    p.write_text(s.replace("</load_first>", "\n" + LF + "\n</load_first>"))
for rel in ["scribe/agents/arch-auditor"]:
    p = ROOT / "plugins" / (rel + ".md")
    s = p.read_text()
    assert s.count("</load_first>") == 1, rel
    p.write_text(s.replace("</load_first>", LF + "\n</load_first>"))
for rel in ["ranger/agents/recon", "sentinel/agents/recon", "sentinel/agents/verifier",
            "scribe/agents/drift-checker", "scribe/agents/verifier", "muse/agents/explorer"]:
    p = ROOT / "plugins" / (rel + ".md")
    s = p.read_text()
    assert "<load_first>" not in s, rel
    assert s.count("\n<backstory>") == 1, rel
    p.write_text(s.replace("\n<backstory>", "\n<load_first>\n" + LF + "\n</load_first>\n\n<backstory>", 1))

# Catalog
p = ROOT / "harnesses/codex/catalog.json"
s = p.read_text()
s = s.replace('"shared/references/architecture/modes.md"]\n    },\n    {\n      "id": "navigator"',
              '"shared/references/architecture/modes.md", "shared/references/tooling/context.md"]\n    },\n    {\n      "id": "navigator"', 1)
s = s.replace('"shared/references/workspace/conventions.md"\n      ]', '"shared/references/workspace/conventions.md",\n        "shared/references/tooling/context.md"\n      ]', 1)
s = s.replace('"shared/references/architecture/typescript.md", "shared/references/workspace/conventions.md"]\n    },\n    {\n      "id": "sentinel",\n      "runtime_files": ["shared/schemas/verdict@3.json"]',
              '"shared/references/architecture/typescript.md", "shared/references/workspace/conventions.md", "shared/references/tooling/context.md"]\n    },\n    {\n      "id": "sentinel",\n      "runtime_files": ["shared/schemas/verdict@3.json", "shared/references/tooling/context.md"]', 1)
p.write_text(s)
print(s.count(CTX))

---
name: sketch
description: >-
  Use this, rather than describing options in prose, whenever the user wants to see options before deciding: "show me some options", "try a few directions", "sketch this", "what could this look like", "I want to see it before we spec it". Builds and renders three structurally different options as an option-set@1 with a decision log. Non-binding: no gate, spec or tests. Stops before implementing; use promote to build.
version: 1.0.0
---

# Muse — Sketch Skill

<overview>
Lets the user see options before anything is decided. The output is a sketch: a small set of structurally different options, each built as a quick static page, rendered, shown, and recorded with a status and a reason. Nothing here is binding. There is no gate, no spec and no test requirement, unfinished ideas and open questions are welcome, and the skill stops before implementing. Open the reply with "Mode: sketch. Nothing here is binding."
</overview>

<dispatch>
| Agent | Model / Effort | Delegate When |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **explorer** | sonnet / medium | An option needs building and rendering in its own context. Up to three explorers may run in parallel, one per option. For a single small option, build it directly instead. |

The explorer is internal to this skill. Do not call it on its own, and never ask it to rank the options.
</dispatch>

<references>
`shared/references/architecture/modes.md`, `shared/schemas/option-set@1.json`

When running render or build commands, keep command output and scripts out of the thread as `shared/references/tooling/context.md` says. Look at one render at a time.
</references>

<io>
**Consumes**: free-text intent, an existing `option-set@1` to continue, or a `requirement@1` for context
**Produces**: `option-set@1` written to `docs/sketches/<id>.json` (`fidelity: sketch`), with working files under `.scratch/<id>/`
</io>

<record_shape>
```json
{
  "id": "SKETCH-001",
  "title": "Hero section",
  "brief": { "problem": "string", "audience": "string", "constraints": ["string"], "non_goals": ["string"] },
  "direction": "string",
  "status": "exploring",
  "round": 1,
  "options": [
    {
      "id": "OPT-split",
      "title": "string",
      "summary": "string",
      "structure": "what makes it structurally different from the others",
      "status": "open",
      "assumptions": ["string"],
      "open_questions": ["string"],
      "renders": [{ "kind": "file", "location": ".scratch/SKETCH-001/OPT-split/index.html", "viewport": "1440x900", "theme": "light" }]
    }
  ],
  "decisions": [{ "option_id": "OPT-split", "decision": "chosen", "reason": "string", "date": "2026-10-20" }],
  "fidelity": "sketch",
  "reasoning": "string"
}
```

Follow it exactly, because the file is checked against `option-set@1` and a record in another shape is rejected. Required: `id` (`SKETCH-` and three or more digits), `title`, `brief` (with `problem` and `audience`), `status` (`exploring`, `decided` or `abandoned`), `round` (an integer from 1), `options` (one to five), `fidelity` (always `sketch`) and `reasoning`. Each option needs `id` (`OPT-` and a lowercase slug), `title`, `summary`, `structure` and `status` (`open`, `parked`, `chosen` or `rejected`); every status except `open` needs a `reason`. A `decided` sketch needs at least one `decisions` entry, and each entry needs `option_id`, `decision`, `reason` and a `YYYY-MM-DD` date. `kind` in a render is `file`, `url` or `screenshot`. No other fields are allowed.
</record_shape>

<workflow>
1. **State the mode, and check it fits.** Begin your first message with exactly: "Mode: sketch. Nothing here is binding." If the work is a shared component, something other code depends on, or behavior and accessibility that must not regress, say the gated path (`muse/component`) fits better and let the user choose.
2. **Write the anchor brief**: the problem, the audience, the constraints (brand, stack, tokens, real content) and the non-goals. Ask at most three short questions, and only when an answer would change the options; otherwise state your assumptions and go on.
3. **Commit a direction** (design work, first round only). Propose four distinct, concrete directions, one line each, and let the user pick one; if they say "you choose", pick and say why. Skip this for non-visual exploration. Later rounds stay inside the chosen direction.
4. **Plan the round.** Name three structural bets (five at most) that differ in arrangement, interaction model or information hierarchy, not in color or spacing. If two options differ only in tint, replace one.
5. **Build each option** as a minimal static page (HTML and CSS, no build step) under `.scratch/<id>/<option-id>/`, using the brief's real content and tokens. Mark placeholder text as placeholder; never invent numbers, claims or testimonials. Use the `explorer` for parallel builds.
6. **Render, then show.** Capture each option at the viewports and themes the brief names (default 390x844 and 1440x900, and light and dark when the project has both) with the project's own Playwright script, a browser tool, or the host's browser. Write `.scratch/<id>/board.html` that lists each option's title, status, summary and renders side by side. Make each preview frame tall enough to show the whole option (at least 640px) and let the board scroll; a clipped preview hides the design. Present the renders before explaining them. If nothing can render, say so plainly and give the one command that opens the files; do not describe a render you did not see.
7. **Record the decision.** The user chooses, rejects or parks. Set each option's `status` with a `reason`, and append an entry with the date to `decisions`; never rewrite an earlier entry or reuse an option id. For another round, re-read the anchor brief, restate it in a line, and generate new options inside the direction. After about four rounds restate the brief and start from it, because options drift.
8. **Close and stop.** Set `status` to `decided` or `abandoned`, write `docs/sketches/<id>.json`, and list the assumptions and open questions. Do not start building. Offer the next step: another round, `muse/promote` to carry the chosen option into real work, or drop it. End with one line naming what was skipped: "Skipped by design: spec, tests and gates."
</workflow>

<rules>
- Write only under `.scratch/<id>/` and to `docs/sketches/<id>.json`. Never edit existing source, configuration or specs. Suggest adding `.scratch/` to the ignore file.
- Keep option ids stable and never reuse one for a different option.
- Do not advocate. Present the options and their trade-offs; the user decides. Give a recommendation only when asked.
- A sketch is never evidence for a gate. Anything that continues goes through `muse/promote`.
- Allowed here and not in a spec: open questions, unverified assumptions, placeholder content, a rough build.
</rules>

<circuit_breaker>
There is no gate to loop on. After five rounds without a decision, say so and offer to narrow the brief, park the exploration, or abandon it.
</circuit_breaker>

It returned one `new` entry for one outcome: a lead line on the link, then what you see and where, the limit that a changeset pushed straight to the branch gets no link, the optional `pr` field for scripts, and that upgrading needs no action. It classified the change as a minor new capability. It did not write the "why it helps" as a separate bullet but put it in the lead line.

**Finding: `shared/...` reference paths depend on the working directory.** In that run the agent reported it could not find `shared/references/delivery/changesets.md` and fell back to the schema-implied rules. This is separate from, and in addition to, the dangling-symlink install defect fixed in the marketplace sources (VERIFY-3 section 7): even a correct install leaves a relative `shared/...` path unresolvable from a user's project. It likely explains the pilots where schema files were not readable at run time. Not fixed here. Options: pass the plugin root into the skill and agent instructions if the host substitutes it, name the references in the skill body so they load with it, or inline the few rules an agent cannot work without. Needs a host check first.

`pr-narrator` and `commit-analyzer` were then changed to match: they follow the repository's own conventions (a pull request template, recent commit scopes and subject style), keep limits in the body instead of the scratchpad, mark breaking changes to command output, exit codes and file formats, and the narrator names or recommends a changeset. One live run of both on the same PR 483 diff: the PR body followed the template sections, put four limits under a "Limits a reader will hit" list, said the tests were not run and gave commands, and added a Changeset section. Two weaknesses: the narrator stated an inferred behavior (shallow clones give no link and no error) as fact while its scratchpad called it an inference, which a new rule now forbids; and the haiku commit body described the mechanism and omitted the direct-push limit, which is not fixed (a commit body is short and the limit belongs in the changeset and PR). Both agents again could not find their `shared/` reference, the working-directory finding above.

Track D is done and committed locally on branch worktree-agent-ab6da94b57c991345. I did not push or bump versions. `just check` exited 0 and `just marketplace-sync` exited 0, run after the final edit. The new `python3 -m unittest tests.test_skill_routing` run exited 0 earlier, before the README edits. `just check` ran after them and covers the full test set.

**Setup:** the worktree did not contain b08a1b0b, so I merged `worktree-frontend-design-evaluation`. The merge commit needed GPG, so I ran it with the sandbox disabled, as authorised.

**What changed**

*Routing wording (13 skills, 4 plugins, all 450 characters or fewer)*
- Descriptions now lead with the situation and request phrases.
- "Use this, not a freehand ..." appears only for ranger/audit, sentinel/gate, muse/component, scribe/draft-spec, scribe/audit-spec and scribe/gate-spec.
- scribe/correct-spec says "instead of editing the spec by hand". muse/sketch says "rather than describing options in prose".
- The read-only or bridging skills make no freehand claim: spec-drift, audit-architecture, verify-spec, architect and promote.
- muse/sketch and muse/promote had been over 450 characters and are now under.
- Codex descriptions got the same phrase for ranger/audit, sentinel/gate, component, draft-spec, audit-spec, gate-spec and sketch.
- One "you are about to do this by hand: invoke X first" bullet was added to the "When to Use" lists in the ranger, sentinel, muse and scribe READMEs.

*Context hygiene*
- One sentence routing `shared/references/tooling/context.md` was added to these skills:
  - ranger/audit
  - sentinel/gate (framework_references)
  - muse/sketch (references; also says look at one render at a time)
  - scribe/audit-architecture
  - scribe/spec-drift
- `<load_first>` now loads it in these agents:
  - ranger: scanner, boundary-tracer, adversary (appended to the existing block) and recon (new block).
  - sentinel: recon and verifier (new blocks).
  - scribe: arch-auditor (appended), drift-checker and verifier (new blocks).
  - muse: explorer (new block).
- The Codex counterparts got the same sentence in their bodies, and the reference is in the Codex catalog `runtime_files` for ranger, sentinel, muse and scribe.
- The sync generated the new `dist/` copies; I did not hand-edit `dist/` or `.agents/`.

*Muse body weight:* I trimmed one redundant overview sentence in sketch. Every rule and the inline record shape are untouched. The skill was already tight, so there was little to cut.

*Test:* `tests/test_skill_routing.py` checks four things.
- All 13 descriptions are at most 450 characters.
- The five command-running skills (ranger/audit, sentinel/gate, muse/sketch, scribe/audit-architecture, scribe/spec-drift) reference context.md in both the Claude and Codex skill files.
- The Codex catalog lists context.md for each plugin that loads it.
- The five read-only skills in the no-freehand set (spec-drift, audit-architecture, verify-spec, architect, promote) do not say "freehand" in the Claude description or the Codex description line. The four freehand-replacing skills (audit, gate, component, draft-spec) do say it.

I also added a Track D entry to `docs/evaluations/frontend-design/IMPLEMENTATION-LOG.md`.

**Not verified**
- I cannot measure whether the new wording raises invocation rates. That needs a transcript comparison after release.
- I did not run a pilot of the changed agents.
- The agent tests only cover descriptions and routing. The `<load_first>` additions in agents are not asserted by any test.

**Decisions for the owner**
1. Ranger and sentinel exit-gates were left alone, as track B owns them. ranger/exit-gate runs commands, so it may want the same `<load_first>` sentence once track B lands.
2. The new `load_first` paths are `shared/...`, relative to the plugin root. The courier finding in the implementation log says this form can fail to resolve from a user's project. These additions share that risk until the path-resolution work lands.
3. Whether the freehand-claim set is right is a judgment call. I treated code review, verification and spec drafting, review and gating as having a real freehand alternative. I treated spec-drift, audit-architecture, verify-spec, architect and promote as not. Edit the sets at the top of the test file to change it.
4. Versions and CHANGELOGs for the four plugins still need bumping by the lead.
